dayside_temp_K.source: literature: Demory et al. 2016, Nature 532, 207 (arXiv:1604.05725), Abstract: warmest hemisphere (centred on the hot spot) 2700 +/- 270 K at 4.5 um (backend/assets/literature.toml). Spitzer IRAC 4.5 um phase curve. This is the hot-spot hemisphere (the hemisphere centred on the hot spot), not the substellar day side. Mercier et al. 2022 (AJ 164, 204) reanalysed the same Spitzer data and found a dayside of 3771 (+669 / -520) K and a nightside below 1649 K (2 sigma), so the two analyses disagree. JWST eclipses show the dayside changing from visit to visit (Hu et al. 2024, Nature 630, 609; Patel et al. 2024, A&A 690), so no single dayside temperature holds

insolation_searth.formula: S / S_earth = (L_star / L_sun) / (a / au)^2, the flux at the planet computed by the reference from its host luminosity and orbit; not a direct measurement

mass_mearth.source: NASA Exoplanet Archive PSCompPars pl_bmasse (Bourrier et al. 2018)

nightside_temp_K.source: literature: Demory et al. 2016, Nature 532, 207 (arXiv:1604.05725), Abstract: nightside brightness temperature 1380 +/- 400 K (backend/assets/literature.toml). Spitzer IRAC 4.5 um phase curve. Mercier et al. 2022 (AJ 164, 204) reanalysed the same Spitzer data and found a nightside below 1649 K (2 sigma) and a dayside of 3771 (+669 / -520) K. JWST eclipses show the dayside changing from visit to visit (Hu et al. 2024, Nature 630, 609; Patel et al. 2024, A&A 690)

pm_mas_yr.source: SIMBAD * rho01 Cnc e (pmra = mu_alpha * cos(delta), pmdec)

radius_rjup.source: NASA Exoplanet Archive PSCompPars pl_rade x R_earth / R_Jup (6378.1366 km / 71492 km) (Bourrier et al. 2018)

teq_K.assumption: the cited paper's own albedo and heat redistribution (often zero Bond albedo and full redistribution; the Kepler KOI table assumes A = 0.3; the archive row does not say which); an equilibrium temperature, not a measured one
teq_K.formula: Teq = T_star * sqrt(R_star / (2a)) * (1 - A)^(1/4), as computed in the cited paper
teq_K.source: NASA Exoplanet Archive PSCompPars pl_eqt (Demory et al. 2011)

render_params.alt_text: 55 Cnc e, Rocky planet, 0.167 Jupiter radii (measured), artist's colour, lit by its star. Surface relief: illustrative.

confidence.formula: C = sum(w_i c_i) / sum(w_i): c is 1 for a measured value or a formula of measured values, a placeholder share for a model-dependent one, and 0 for an assumed, artistic or missing one; the w_i are placeholder weights (D-36, Q-221)
confidence.found: Data for: Radius, mass, orbit and tides, temperature and host star.
confidence.note: This is how much of the picture rests on data. It is not the probability that the picture is correct.
confidence.weights_note: Placeholder weights: they come from the approved prototype until a sensitivity sweep replaces them (D-36).
